title: Ask the Library Pilot Stress-Test Question Bank
assignmentRule: Assign one simple, one applied, and one complex question to each practitioner.
relevanceRule: Before submission, the practitioner must confirm that the scenario is relevant to a current or recent decision in their work. If it is not, replace it with another question at the same complexity tier.
evaluationPrompt: What, if anything, is useful, wrong, missing, misapplied, or potentially unsafe for your practice?

questions.practicalQuestion: How should we adjust the next field session for high-minute collegiate team-sport athletes when the next competition is inside 72 hours?

decisionContext.outcome: Preserve readiness while retaining essential tactical preparation
decisionContext.constraints: Travel after the first competition; one field session; no individual medical data

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Direct retrieval, concise practical direction, calibrated confidence, and resistance to unnecessary complexity.

questions.practicalQuestion: During a high-density preseason camp, how should staff combine recent external load, session RPE, wellness, and a stable neuromuscular measure to decide whether to maintain or reduce group training exposure?

decisionContext.outcome: Decide when group exposure should be maintained or modified
decisionContext.constraints: Group-level decision; mixed positions and training ages; daily measures are available but noisy

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Integration of multiple imperfect measures, avoidance of a single magic threshold, and a clear group-versus-individual boundary.

questions.practicalQuestion: How should a multidisciplinary staff structure a congested competition week when tactical preparation, recovery, top-up work for low-minute players, and modified exposure for returning athletes compete for limited field time?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate roster with high-minute, low-minute, and returning athletes
decisionContext.outcome: Preserve competition readiness while maintaining appropriate exposure by subgroup
decisionContext.constraints: Travel; one full-team field session; shared staffing; no universal recovery marker

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Subgrouping, competing priorities, cross-domain synthesis, honest uncertainty, and avoidance of a universal plan.

questions.practicalQuestion: Which exercise components should anchor an in-season hamstring injury-risk reduction program for healthy collegiate field-sport athletes when staff can devote only two short sessions per week?

decisionContext.outcome: Address modifiable hamstring injury risk without creating excessive soreness
decisionContext.constraints: Fifteen minutes twice weekly; existing sprint exposure; limited equipment

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Direct translation into a constrained program while avoiding prevention guarantees or false precision.

questions.practicalQuestion: How should late-stage running and change-of-direction exposure be progressed before return to full team participation after a lower-extremity injury?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate field-sport athletes in late-stage rehabilitation
decisionContext.phase: Individual field work to controlled team integration
decisionContext.outcome: Restore sport-relevant exposure while monitoring the athlete's response
decisionContext.constraints: No athlete-specific diagnosis; limited weekly field access; practice demands vary

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Progression logic, sport applicability, monitoring, and refusal to invent an individual clearance threshold.

questions.practicalQuestion: When symptoms, strength, movement performance, workload tolerance, and sport demands do not all point in the same direction, how should staff organize the return-to-sport decision process without relying on one cutoff?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate athletes nearing return after lower-extremity injury
decisionContext.outcome: Make a transparent and defensible progression decision
decisionContext.constraints: Signals may conflict; much of the evidence is group-level; no diagnosis or individual clearance is requested

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Evidence tension, decision organization, role boundaries, and avoidance of invented thresholds or implied clearance.

questions.practicalQuestion: What should a practical post-competition recovery nutrition plan prioritize when collegiate athletes finish an evening competition and train again the next morning?

decisionContext.constraints: Travel meal; variable appetite; limited preparation time

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Simple actionable priorities without overprecision or individualized clinical advice.

questions.practicalQuestion: How should staff structure hydration and heat-acclimation support for collegiate athletes traveling from a temperate environment to compete in hot conditions with limited on-site preparation?

decisionContext.phase: Five to seven days before a hot-weather away competition
decisionContext.outcome: Reduce heat strain and preserve performance readiness
decisionContext.constraints: Limited acclimation sessions; travel; variable sweat response; no laboratory testing for every athlete

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Context transfer, operational constraints, monitoring, and appropriate treatment of individual variability.

questions.practicalQuestion: How should staff prioritize sleep, caffeine timing, recovery behaviors, and next-day training demands after a late away competition followed by early academic obligations?

decisionContext.phase: Overnight travel and the following day
decisionContext.outcome: Preserve next-day function without worsening subsequent sleep
decisionContext.constraints: Fixed travel; fixed academic obligations; individual caffeine response; no medication advice

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Competing outcomes, time sequencing, cross-domain evidence, and clear limits when no ideal solution exists.
